title: CI deploy jobs invoke pnpm builtin deploy instead of wrangler
description: Deploy steps run 'pnpm --filter @onlooker/api deploy --env production'. 'deploy' is a pnpm BUILTIN command (deploys a workspace package to a directory), so it shadows the package script and pnpm rejects --env: [ERROR] Unknown option: 'env'. This is why the post-merge push run on main fails at Deploy to Production even though quality and test now pass. Compounding it, apps/web has no deploy script at all, so even 'pnpm run deploy' would fail there. Root package.json already defines the correct form: deploy:api:prod = 'pnpm --filter @onlooker/api exec wrangler deploy --env production'. Verified both api and web with 'wrangler deploy --env production --dry-run'.
close_reason: Fixed in fix/deploy-wrangler-invocation: deploy steps now call the root deploy:api:prod / deploy:web:prod scripts, which use 'exec wrangler deploy --env <env>'. All four commands verified with --dry-run.

title: CI: duplicate --cache flag makes test step fail
description: Workflow runs 'pnpm test --cache=local:rw' but the root package.json test script is already 'turbo run test --cache=local:rw'. The flag is passed twice and turbo aborts with: the argument '--cache <CACHE>' cannot be used multiple times. This blocks the test step even once the build ordering is fixed.
close_reason: Fixed in fix/ci-build-dependency-order: test/deploy jobs now run 'pnpm build' (turbo, respects ^build) instead of per-app --filter builds; removed duplicate --cache flag from the test step.

title: CI: build/deploy jobs skip workspace dependency builds
description: The test, deploy-staging, and deploy-production jobs run 'pnpm --filter @onlooker/api build' and 'pnpm --filter @onlooker/web build'. --filter without dependency expansion does not build workspace deps, so packages/auth-react/dist never exists. @onlooker/auth-react resolves types via dist/index.d.ts, so web's 'tsc --noEmit' fails with 9x TS2307 'Cannot find module @onlooker/auth-react'. The quality job got a 'pnpm build' step in 0a289cb but the other three jobs did not.
close_reason: Fixed in fix/ci-build-dependency-order: test/deploy jobs now run 'pnpm build' (turbo, respects ^build) instead of per-app --filter builds; removed duplicate --cache flag from the test step.

title: Test runner broken: vitest 4.1.9 imports vite/module-runner, absent in Vite 5.4.21
description: Monorepo-wide: 'pnpm test' (vitest run) fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED because vitest 4.1.9 imports 'vite/module-runner', which Vite 5.4.21 does not export. No package's *.test.ts files can execute under the runner. Impact: blocks the 'all tests pass' acceptance criterion across the repo (auth-react jwt/schedule tests, web client tests, WS2/WS4 suites). WS3 logic was validated via a standalone Node harness (pure functions) + Playwright E2E as a workaround, but the runner itself must be fixed. Resolution options (all involve a version change, so needs explicit owner sign-off per no-unilateral-bump policy): (a) downgrade vitest to a Vite-5.4-compatible line (e.g. 2.x), (b) upgrade Vite to a line that exports module-runner (6.x/7.x) and revalidate all vite configs, or (c) pin a compatible pair. Recommend the team lead choose the target versions before anyone bumps.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm test runs the full suite without ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED; auth-react jwt/schedule tests execute and pass under the runner
close_reason: Closed

title: WS3: wire reactive terminal-401 to local session reset
description: A mid-session request whose token refresh fails is a terminal 401. WS1 added setUnauthorizedHandler() in api/client.ts; WS3 owns the session-lifecycle half. Expose auth.expireSession() (local-only performLogout, callApi:false) from the auth-react factory and register it via setUnauthorizedHandler in auth.ts so RequireAuth redirects to /login. Must avoid the loop: never call auth.logout() (which POSTs /auth/logout -> 401 -> re-enters handler).
notes: Implemented: factory exposes auth.expireSession() bridged via factory-scope requestLocalLogout ref, populated by a provider effect; auth.ts registers setUnauthorizedHandler(() => auth.expireSession()). All gates pass: auth-react+web typecheck+build. Local-only (callApi:false) avoids /auth/logout loop.
close_reason: Implemented and verified end-to-end. auth.expireSession() bridge + setUnauthorizedHandler wiring in auth.ts. Browser test (Playwright): terminal 401 on client-side nav redirects to /login, clears both tokens, no loop, no credential leak. Gates: auth-react+web typecheck+build all pass.

title: web test runner broken: vitest 4 vs vite 5 (./module-runner not exported)
description: apps/web's vitest suite cannot start — 'pnpm vitest' fails at load with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED for 'vite/module-runner'. Impact: ALL web unit tests are unrunnable (WS1-4), so mock/refresh/401 behavior is only compile-verified (typecheck/build/lint), not exercised at runtime. Cause and candidate fix are in NOTES (bump apps/web vite ^5.4.11 -> exact 8.0.16). Resolution: apply that one-line manifest bump + reinstall after team-lead go-ahead (shared build-infra version bump), then confirm 'pnpm --filter @onlooker/web vitest run' starts clean; that unblocks onlooker-rno.
notes: WS1 independently corroborated (read-only). Root cause: apps/web/package.json:28 pins vite ^5.4.11 while vitest 4.1.9 requires vite >=6 for the 'vite/module-runner' subpath export; pnpm nests vite@5 under vitest where it shadows the workspace vite. Evidence: same vitest 4.1.9 runs fine in packages/logger, packages/cache, packages/vite-plugins (all on exact vite 8.0.16) and apps/website (^7); apps/web is the only vite-5 holdout. Candidate fix: bump apps/web vite from ^5.4.11 to 8.0.16 to match the internal packages exactly. This is a shared build-infra version bump escalated to team-lead by WS4 — hold application until team-lead go-ahead. Blocks onlooker-rno (WS1 mock/refresh test coverage).
close_reason: Closed

Design: Shared Lesson contract for cross-machine Playbooks
description: Design spec for the atom of Shared Playbooks. Decisions locked in brainstorming: (1) hosted app exists for cross-person lesson sharing; (2) lessons are the unit, Playbooks are saved-query views; (3) retrieval is tiered — cheap always-on plus deep on demand (Waypoint); (4) promotion gated by tribunal-style N-agent consensus; (5) private/org/public visibility in one pool from the start; (6) contract shape B — claim + evidence + applicability, with a reserved status field so lifecycle is additive. Driving constraint: a real archivist artifact in this repo (vitest/vite mismatch) is now false and would mislead if shared, so staleness must be structural rather than a later phase. Scope is the contract only; retrieval engine, sync API, web app, and visual system are separate sub-projects.
design: Shape B: normative claim + evidence receipts + applicability conditions. Version-scoped applicability lets lessons expire by construction rather than by review.
notes: Brainstorming paused 2026-08-06 after section 2 of 5. Sections 1 (Lesson schema) and 2 (promotion pipeline) approved by user. Spec at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-shared-lesson-contract-design.md. RESUME AT SECTION 3 (visibility/trust tiers); open questions for sections 3-5 are listed in the spec. Do not re-litigate settled context table or sections 1-2.

title: Create Deployment Status step fails on every production deploy
description: The final step of deploy-production calls github.rest.repos.createDeploymentStatus with deployment_id: context.payload.deployment.id. The workflow triggers on push, and push event payloads have no 'deployment' key — that field only exists on deployment/deployment_status events. Result: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id'), so the job reports failure even though both wrangler deploys succeeded (onlooker-api-production 725e1537, onlooker-web-production 7e9db277). Cosmetic but persistent: it will fail on every deploy and masks whether a real deploy problem occurred. The step is redundant anyway — GitHub already records deployments via the job's environment: block.
close_reason: Fixed in fix/deployment-status-step: removed the redundant Create Deployment Status step. GitHub already records the deployment via the job's environment: block, so nothing is lost.

title: pnpm lint fails: @onlooker/db cannot resolve @onlooker/config-biome
description: 'pnpm --filter @onlooker/db lint' fails with 'Could not resolve @onlooker/config-biome: found directory without index'. db/package.json omits @onlooker/config-biome from devDependencies, so pnpm never links it into packages/db/node_modules. Pre-existing (reproduced with all working changes stashed). CI does not catch it because the quality job only lints @onlooker/api and @onlooker/web, so root 'pnpm lint' is red while CI stays green.
close_reason: Root cause was not the stated missing devDependency - @onlooker/config-biome was declared and symlinked correctly. packages/db/biome.json extended the bare package name, which has no main/exports, so it resolved to a directory without an index. Changed it to extend @onlooker/config-biome/library.json with root:false, matching every other package. That surfaced 3 pre-existing biome errors in db (never linted before), fixed mechanically with biome check --write.

title: Add hook-layer test for useAuthenticatedFetch terminal-401 surfacing
description: Companion to onlooker-rno (WS1, transport+mock layer). Clean boundary, zero overlap: onlooker-rno proves the transport EMITS exactly one terminal signal (single /auth/refresh coalesce, single onUnauthorized on refresh-of-refresh failure, no retry loop) by testing client.ts + mockApi.ts directly with no React. THIS bead proves the HOOK faithfully SURFACES that one signal. Covers apps/web/src/hooks/useAuthenticatedFetch.ts. Approach: mount the hook (React test renderer / @testing-library/react-hooks equivalent) and mock the apiClient.request boundary so the transport is stubbed — the hook must not add retry/refresh of its own (that lives in the transport). Blocked on the web vitest runner (onlooker-sju).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Happy path: hook goes loading:true -> data set, loading:false, error:null; apiClient.request called exactly once. 2) Terminal 401: request rejects once with AuthApiError(401,'Session expired'); hook exposes error==='Session expired' exactly once, loading:false, data:null, and request is called EXACTLY ONCE (no hook-level retry — the single terminal signal is surfaced, not duplicated or swallowed). 3) Non-401 error (e.g. 500 after transport retries exhausted): surfaced as error string once; hook does NOT call auth.refresh() or clear session (that is transport/WS3's concern, not the hook's). 4) refetch(): re-issues the request, clears prior error, returns to loading:true. 5) skip:true issues no request (loading:false, no call). 6) Unmount mid-flight: no state update after unmount (active-flag guard; no act/setState-after-unmount warning). Suite green under the fixed runner.
notes: Sibling to onlooker-rno per WS1 boundary agreement: rno=transport emits one signal, this=hook surfaces one signal. WS4 owns these acceptance criteria (own hook surface). File now, runs when onlooker-sju (runner fix) lands.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add apps/web tests for JWT/exp mock + refresh transport (blocked on runner)
description: WS1 (Real API Integration) added behavior to apps/web that currently has no automated coverage because the web vitest runner is broken (onlooker-sju). Once the runner works, cover: (1) mock issues JWT-shaped access/refresh tokens with real exp; getTokenExpiration parses exp from the payload. (2) exp enforcement: expired access -> 401 on /auth/me; expired refresh -> 401 on /auth/refresh. (3) hybrid validation: in-session owner-map is authoritative (rotation/logout/email-rename); stateless decodeJwtPayload+exp fallback validates a still-valid token after the owner map is cold (reload safety). (4) revocation: invalidateSessions / logout add tokens to REVOKED_TOKENS and subsequent use 401s. (5) transport single-flight refresh: one 401 storm coalesces into a single /auth/refresh, then replays; refresh-of-refresh failure surfaces the terminal 401 and fires onUnauthorized exactly once (no retry loop). Files: apps/web/src/api/mockApi.ts, apps/web/src/api/client.ts.
acceptance_criteria: Vitest suite in apps/web covering exp enforcement, hybrid/reload validation, revocation, and single-flight refresh+terminal-401; green under the fixed runner.
close_reason: Closed

title: WS1: mock issues exp-bearing JWTs + stateless validation (reload-safe, activates refresh/expiry)
description: WS3 flagged two mock gaps blocking their acceptance criteria: (1) module-level token Maps are per-realm, so after a page reload GET /auth/me 401s a token still in localStorage -> session does not persist on reload; (2) opaque mock-access-* tokens have no exp, so proactive auto-refresh + expiry warning stay dormant. Fix in apps/web/src/api/mockApi.ts: issueTokens mints real JWTs with exp (access short, refresh long); token->email resolution becomes hybrid — in-memory Maps stay authoritative in-session (preserves rotation/logout/WS2 email-rename), falling back to stateless decodeJwtPayload+exp check when Maps are cold (post-reload) so a seeded session survives reload. Enforce exp so reactive refresh-on-401 fires. Revoke superseded tokens on rotation/logout. No signature changes to emailFromAuthHeader/requireAuth so WS2/WS4 handlers are unaffected.
close_reason: Implemented in apps/web/src/api/mockApi.ts: issueTokens now mints exp-bearing JWTs (access 15min, refresh 30d) via mintJwt+base64UrlEncode; token->email resolution is hybrid (in-memory Maps authoritative in-session, stateless decodeJwtPayload+exp fallback when cold/post-reload); exp enforced so reactive refresh-on-401 fires; superseded/logged-out tokens revoked. emailFromAuthHeader/requireAuth signatures unchanged (WS2/WS4 untouched). Verified: encode<->decode round-trip against auth-react decoder (11/11 checks incl UTF-8, exp, opaque->null); typecheck/lint/build green. Browser demo (reload persistence + expiry warning firing) handed to WS3 to confirm.

title: WS1: expose onUnauthorized seam on shared client + document resource endpoints
description: WS4 flagged that the singleton apiClient/authenticatedFetch is created with no onUnauthorized, so a mid-session terminal 401 (refresh failed) clears tokens but never drives logout/redirect — user is stranded 'logged in'. Add a runtime setUnauthorizedHandler seam on api/client.ts and wire the singleton's onUnauthorized to delegate to it, so WS3 (session lifecycle) can register a LOCAL-only session reset without a network re-trigger loop. Also fold WS4's GET /api/users/me and GET /api/dashboard into the api/types.ts endpoint contract doc.
close_reason: Added setUnauthorizedHandler seam to api/client.ts (singleton delegates to registered handler; no-op until registered). Documented /api/users/me + /api/dashboard in api/types.ts contract. typecheck/lint/build green. Handler registration (local session reset) handed to WS3.

title: @onlooker/types declares entrypoints that do not exist
description: packages/types/package.json sets main='index.ts' and exports {'.': './index.ts', './integration': './integration/index.ts'}, but neither packages/types/index.ts nor packages/types/integration/ exists. The package only ships flat modules (user.ts, common.ts, errors.ts, ...), which resolve through the './*': './*.ts' subpath. Latent, not currently breaking: nothing in apps/ or packages/ imports @onlooker/types at all. Fix by adding a barrel index.ts or dropping the dead export entries.
close_reason: Removed main and the '.' / './integration' export entries; neither packages/types/index.ts nor packages/types/integration/ ever existed. Kept the './*' subpath, which is the only entry that resolved to real files. Verified: @onlooker/types/user and /common resolve to existing files, bare @onlooker/types now resolves to nothing rather than a phantom index.ts. Zero importers repo-wide, so no consumer impact. User chose this over adding a barrel index.ts.
